translation:
Kashi

_Kashi manhe Kabirki abha, Patan manhe Shri Padmanabha ||55||_
_So Sadguru Jivan pragate aaye, sab santan man vanchhitpaye ||56||_
(In Kashi was your radiance as Kabir, and in Patan Shri Padmanabh; that same Sadguru Jivan has manifested and come, and all the saints have obtained the desire of their hearts.)

In Kashi, your (Jivanji-Krishna's) form was present as a shadow-form under the guise of Kabir, and in Patan you were Shri Padmanabh — you, the same Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj, have appeared as the one dear to the minds of all saints. Thus all the saints have attained you, who are dear to the minds of all of them.

Jivanji Maharaj manifested in Kashi as Sadguru Kabir, and Jivanji Maharaj has affirmed Kabirji as Sadguru. In Patan, Kabirji was also the guru of Bhagwan Padmanabh. Thus the Lord manifested at one and the same time in two forms — as Kabir and as Padmanabh. The Lord's divine play (lila) is wondrous. At the churning of the ocean, the Lord took on three avatars simultaneously: in the form of Vishnu he wedded Lakshmi; in the form of Kurma (the tortoise) he upheld Mount Meru; in the form of Mohini he gave the nectar to the gods to drink. The importance of Kashi for Sadguru Kabirji is as the battlefield where he confronted the followers of the path of ritual works (karma-margis). It is the land of the Sadguru's manifestation.
